endings.title: Albert Needs a Minute
endings.text: Albert returned {cat} with a three-page handwritten care guide, all 14 toys and a heartfelt apology to the volunteer. He visits on Saturdays. He's started fostering kittens instead, which is somehow more chaotic.

endings.title: Achoo and Goodbye
endings.text: {owner} lasted until the 40th sneeze and the third box of tissues. "It's not you, it's my sinuses." {cat} accepts this. The shelter's air purifier is very nice, actually.

endings.title: Voted Off the Island
endings.text: There was a household meeting. {partner} brought a slideshow. {cat} was returned 2–0, with one abstention ({cat}, who was asleep).

endings.title: The Dog Won
endings.text: {owner} decided the household "wasn't ready for a cat." {dog} watched you leave from the window, tail low, deeply confused about what just happened. {dog} will think about you every day.

endings.title: Return to Sender
endings.text: {owner} filled out the return form in pen and didn't make eye contact. Back at the shelter, the volunteer gives {cat} a chin scratch and a better cushion. Honestly, a lateral move.

endings.title: It's Me or the Cat
endings.text: {partner} stood in the ruins of the living room and said the line. {owner} took a very long time to answer. Too long. {cat} is going back. {owner} is sleeping on the shredded couch.

endings.title: Lease Violation
endings.text: The landlord did an inspection. He photographed the curtains, the couch and the door frame, then quietly opened the lease to the "Pets" clause. {cat} has been evicted. {owner} has been invoiced.

endings.title: The Deposit Taker
endings.text: {owner} sat on what was left of the couch and did math out loud. The security deposit is gone. So is {cat}, back to the shelter, where there is nothing left to shred.

endings.title: One Leap Too Far
endings.text: {cat} leaped. {cat} missed the pigeon completely and landed, unharmed and dignified, in the downstairs neighbor's herb planter. The downstairs neighbor has now adopted {cat}. The pigeon visits daily, to gloat.

endings.title: Defected for Tuna
endings.text: {cat} never left the armchair. The neighbor buys tuna in oil by the case and has never once owned a vacuum. {owner} waves through the peephole sometimes. {cat} does not wave back.

endings.title: So Close
endings.text: Day 14. {owner} hesitated over the adoption papers, said "I just need a bit more time to think," and handed {cat} back. There's a sticky note on {cat}'s shelter card now: "almost."

endings.title: Not Quite a Match
endings.text: Two weeks are up. {owner} says nice things about {cat}'s "big personality" and signs nothing. The shelter's front window gets a new resident, who is very good at sitting in front windows.

endings.title: Best Friends Forever
endings.text: {owner} signs the papers with {cat} and {dog} asleep in the same dog bed, which is now the cat's bed. {dog} does not mind. {dog} has never been happier.

endings.title: Chicken Nugget Forever
endings.text: Albert signs the papers, cries a little, and announces it to a group chat that already knew. He has ordered a framed portrait of {cat} in a Victorian gentleman's coat. He has ordered two.

endings.title: Suspiciously Perfect
endings.text: Zero broken glasses. Pristine couch. Constant purring. {owner} adopts {cat} immediately and, late at night, wonders what {cat} is planning. {cat} is planning something.

endings.title: Loved Despite Everything
endings.text: The couch is ribbons. The curtains are a memory. {owner} adopts {cat} anyway, from a folding chair, with genuine love and a quote from a carpet cleaner.

endings.title: Ruler of the Household
endings.text: {owner} adopts {cat} and immediately buys a second cat tree, a heated window perch and the expensive pâté. {cat} sleeps in the cardboard box it all came in.

endings.title: Forever Home
endings.text: Day 14. {owner} signs the adoption papers while {cat} sits on them. It's official: {cat} lives here now, and the sunny spot by the window is legally theirs.

endings.title: The Masterpiece
endings.text: Nothing is on any shelf. Nothing is in one piece. {owner} stands in the doorway, speechless, as {cat} sits in the center of it all like an artist at a gallery opening.

endings.title: The Mild Menace
endings.text: TWO WEEKS. WE HAD TWO WEEKS. THE COUCH STILL HAS ITS ARMS. WE ARE ASHAMED. {owner} IS THRILLED. THIS IS THE WORST ENDING.

endings.title: Survivor of the Storm
endings.text: Day 14 arrives and somehow the place is still standing, barely. {owner} has aged a year. {cat} has had the best two weeks of their life.
